title: Al-Battani's observations and Kitab al-Zij at ar-Raqqah
summary: Al-Battani, a native of Harran, made most of his astronomical observations at ar-Raqqah on the Euphrates, with the Fihrist placing them between 877 and 918. His major work, the Kitab al-Zij, has 57 chapters and catalogues 489 stars, and his obliquity of the ecliptic came to 23 degrees 35 minutes.

uncertainty.note: Observation span as given by the Fihrist via MacTutor; Encyclopedia.com says he was active until about 918 and dates his earliest observations to 877. His birth date is given as about 850 (MacTutor) or c. 858 (Encyclopedia.com).

as_recorded.value: he observed between the years 877 and 918
the 877 date that he himself attached to his earliest astronomical observations

where.historical_name: ar-Raqqah on the Euphrates, Abbasid caliphate

importance.justification: A major work of Islamic-world astronomy whose star catalogue and tables are described as among the most valuable of the pre-telescopic era.

sources.title: Abu Abdallah Mohammad ibn Jabir Al-Battani
sources.publisher: MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews

reviewer_note: Least sure of birth dates (about 850 vs c. 858) and the year-length figure (the two sources differ, so it is not claimed). The record covers the observation span and Zij, not his life. The pin is Raqqa, where most observations were made; he also observed at Antioch.
